title: Supported Taylor presentations, intrinsic minors and unit diagram pivots
statement:
Let $L$ be a characteristic-zero field, $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ a finite variable tuple, and $A=L[[X]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_s\in\mathbf N^d$ be distinct coordinatewise minimal vertices ordered by nondecreasing total degree, put $D= igcup_i(a_i+\mathbf N^d)$, $d_i=|a_i|$, and $\Delta_i=\{ eta:a_i+ eta
otin igcup_{j<i}(a_j+\mathbf N^d)\}$. Let $K\subset A$ be an ideal and $f_i\in K$ have order $d_i$. Assume every $h\in K$ admits $h=\sum_iq_if_i$ with $\operatorname{supp}q_i\subset\Delta_i$. Assume also that in every homogeneous degree, and for every prefix consisting of all vertices up to a chosen degree bound, the initial homogeneous forms of its $f_i$ have unique division with quotients supported in the corresponding $\Delta_i$ and remainder outside the prefix diagram. For $t\ge0$, put $T_t=A[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$, $N_t=\#\{\gamma:|\gamma|\le t\}$, $M_t=\sum_{h\in K}T_t h(X+Y)$, and $F_t=T_t/M_t$. Taylor substitution $h\mapsto h(X+Y)$ is a ring homomorphism to $A[[Y]]$, with coefficient $[Y^
u]h(X+Y)=\partial^
u h(X)/
u!$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. The module $M_t$ is the $A$-span of the translates of all $h\in K$, and is generated by the finite supported columns $Y^ eta f_i(X+Y) mod(Y)^{t+1}$ with $ eta\in\Delta_i$, $| eta|\le t$. Let $B'_t$ be their matrix in the monomial basis, and $B_t$ the matrix allowing all $ eta$ of degree at most $t$. Then
$$r_t:=\operatorname{rank}_L B_t(0)=\operatorname{rank}_L B'_t(0)=\#\{\gamma\in D:|\gamma|\le t\}.$$
The columns of $B'_t(0)$ with $| eta|+d_i\le t$, together with the monomial columns indexed outside $D$, form a basis of $L[Y]/(Y)^{t+1}$. The square submatrix $C_t$ on those supported columns and the rows $D\cap\{|\gamma|\le t\}$ has unit determinant in $A$. If $H_t=N_t-r_t>0$, the ideal of $(r_t+1)$-minors [def-trf-minor-ideal] of either $B_t$ or $B'_t$ equals $\operatorname{Fitt}_{H_t-1}(F_t)$, where this is the presentation-independent ideal generated by minors of size $N_t-(H_t-1)$ of a relation matrix. If $H_t=0$ that minors ideal is zero. In either case it is unchanged by replacing $f_i$ by any other finite ideal generators of $K$; for $H_t>0$ its extension along any ring map $A	o A'$ equals the same indexed Fitting ideal of $F_t\otimes_AA'$. Empty families and empty pivots are allowed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94, for the route only; BM Definitions 7.9, 7.12--7.13, Remark 7.11, Lemma 7.7 and unit pivot in Theorem 7.14, pp.265--267; supported presentation in its final paragraph, pp.267--268. proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus] with $W=X$, transverse variables $V$, $\phi(W)=W$, no $T$ variables, and input $h(V)$ independent of $W$. This gives the homomorphism $h\mapsto h(X+Y)$ in the jointly completed ring. Regrouping coefficients identifies $L[[X,Y]]$ with $L[[X]][[Y]]$: both consist of arbitrary families indexed by $(\alpha,
u)$, and each product coefficient is the same finite convolution. Its coefficient formula is $[Y^
u]h(X+Y)=\partial^
u h(X)/
u!$. Reducing modulo $(Y)^{t+1}$ therefore gives a homomorphism $	au_t:A	o T_t$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); formal Taylor substitution

proof.text: Let $V_t$ be the $A$-span of $\tau_t(h)$ for all $h\in K$. It contains those translates and lies in $M_t$. For every $h\in K$, $Y_j\tau_t(h)=\tau_t(X_jh)-X_j\tau_t(h)\in V_t$, since $X_jh\in K$. Thus $V_t$ is stable under multiplication by each $Y_j$ and by $A$, hence by $T_t$, which consists of finite $A$-linear combinations of monomials $Y^\beta$, $|\beta|\le t$. Consequently $V_t=M_t$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); interpretation of the Taylor ideal as an A-module

proof.text: Each $\Delta_i$ is downward closed: if $\eta\le\gamma\in\Delta_i$ and $a_j\le a_i+\eta$ for some $j<i$, then $a_j\le a_i+\gamma$, a contradiction. Choose the assumed supported expansion $h=\sum_iq_if_i$ for $h\in K$. By step 1, $\tau_t(h)=\sum_i\tau_t(q_i)\tau_t(f_i)$. Writing $q_i=\sum_{\gamma\in\Delta_i}c_{i\gamma}X^\gamma$ gives $[Y^\eta]\tau_t(q_i)=\sum_{\gamma\ge\eta}c_{i\gamma}\binom\gamma\eta X^{\gamma-\eta}$; this is a well-defined series, since each $X$ coefficient has just one possible $\gamma$. It is zero unless $\eta\in\Delta_i$, by downward closure. Hence every translate is in the $A$-span of the supported columns. Conversely $Y^\eta\tau_t(f_i)\in V_t$ by step 2. This proves that $B_t$ and $B_t^{\prime}$ both have image $M_t$, and hence cokernel $F_t$. There are only finitely many indices of degree at most $t$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); final paragraph of Theorem 7.14, supported presentation

proof.text: Write $H_i$ for the initial degree-$d_i$ form of $f_i$. Use the hypothesis on the full degree prefix (choose a bound at least every $d_i$). Unique homogeneous division says exactly that in degree $k$ the family $Y^\beta H_i$, $\beta\in\Delta_i$, $|\beta|+d_i=k$, together with the $Y^\gamma$, $\gamma\notin D$, $|\gamma|=k$, is a basis. The corresponding truncated family $Y^\beta f_i(Y)$, $|\beta|+d_i\le t$, together with the outside monomials, is a basis through degree $t$: inductively remove the degree-$k$ component using that homogeneous basis, for $k=0,\ldots,t$. The residual after step $k$ has no terms through degree $k$. For independence, a nonzero relation has a smallest leading degree among its nonzero coefficients; its degree component contradicts independence of the homogeneous family at that degree. This is a finite induction, including degree zero.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); Lemma 7.7 and basis argument for the unit pivot

proof.text: The disjoint sets $a_i+\Delta_i$ partition $D$: assign $\gamma\in D$ to the first $i$ for which $a_i\le\gamma$. Thus the number of supported columns with $|\beta|+d_i\le t$ is $r=\#\{\gamma\in D:|\gamma|\le t\}$. On setting $X=0$, those are the columns in step 4; every other supported column is zero because its least degree exceeds $t$. They are independent, so $\operatorname{rank}B_t^{\prime}(0)=r$. Step 3 implies that the images of $B_t(0)$ and $B_t^{\prime}(0)$ coincide: express each column of either matrix as an $A$-linear combination of the other columns and evaluate coefficients at zero. Therefore both ranks equal $r=r_t$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); rank of the Taylor presentation at zero

proof.text: Adjoin to the $r_t$ supported columns the outside monomial columns. Step 4 says the resulting $N_t\times N_t$ matrix at zero is invertible. Order rows with those in $D$ first and the complementary rows last, and order columns with the supported ones first. Its block form is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix} C_t(0)&0\\ *&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so expansion along the monomial columns gives $\det C_t(0)\ne0$. Evaluation at zero commutes with the finite determinant sum. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring](a), $\det C_t$ is a unit of $A$. This also covers the empty pivot, whose determinant is $1$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), pp.265--268, Definitions 7.12--7.13 and Theorem 7.14 proof (online journal PDF; absent from literature/); unit pivot in the proof of Theorem 7.14

proof.text: For $H_t=N_t-r_t>0$ put $k=H_t-1$, so $N_t-k=r_t+1$. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] to the surjection $A^{N_t}\to F_t$ with kernel $M_t$ established in step 3. Its kernel-row minors equal the $(r_t+1)$-minors of either relation matrix: expand a determinant multilinearly after writing each kernel vector as a finite combination of its generating columns. Terms with repeated columns vanish; the remaining terms are generators of the matrix-minor ideal, up to signs. Conversely each matrix column is a kernel vector. This identifies both ideals with $\operatorname{Fitt}_{H_t-1}(F_t)$ and gives its asserted extension under every $A\to A^{\prime}$ by clause (2) of the cited node. If $H_t=0$, the requested size is $N_t+1$, larger than the number of rows, so the ideal is zero by [def-trf-minor-ideal].

Any other finite generators $g_j$ of $K$ define the same module $M_t$: if $h=\sum_ja_jg_j$, the homomorphism from step 1 gives $\tau_t(h)=\sum_j\tau_t(a_j)\tau_t(g_j)$. Thus their unrestricted monomial columns also present $F_t$. Their images at zero have the same rank $r_t$, by the same evaluated mutual-column expressions as in step 5. For $H_t>0$ apply the presentation independence already cited in step 7; for $H_t=0$ all the minors again have size larger than $N_t$. Empty generators force $K=0$, give rank zero and the ordinary monomial basis. A degree-zero vertex gives $D=\mathbf N^d$ and $H_t=0$; the preceding arguments still apply, also for $d=0$.
